wecom.title: Onboard a corporation
wecom.hint: Click "Generate install link" and send the link or QR code to the corporation's admin to scan/open for approval. On success this system auto-registers the corporation via the create_auth callback (writes wecom_app_profile). The link is generated by WeCom get_customized_auth_url; its validity follows WeCom's response (up to 10 days). The QR code greys out when it expires, so regenerate it.

corp.title: Internal app (self-built)
corp.hint: This deployment connects as an internal app: credentials come from config.yaml (wecom_corp_id / wecom_corp_secret / wecom_corp_agent_id). Fill them in, then click "Verify and connect"; the corporation is registered only after all three checks pass.
corp.callbackHint: Fill this URL into WeCom → Tools → Contacts sync → Set event receiver URL. Leave the app's own message callback empty: the two use different tokens, and pointing both at one URL makes half the payloads fail signature verification.
corp.callbackYes: Configured (member changes sync in real time)
corp.callbackNo: Not configured (full sync only; to get increments, fill Token / EncodingAESKey for this URL in the WeCom console)
corp.connectConfirm: Connect checks: whether the app Secret can fetch a token, whether contacts are readable, and whether any member is visible. Re-run it whenever the Corporation ID / AgentId changed or the Secret was rotated.
corp.connectOk: Connected: {{depts}} departments visible, {{members}} members in the sample department
corp.connectHint: After rotating the app Secret you must click "Verify and connect" again, otherwise every call fails with 40001. How many people get synced depends on the app's visible scope — set it to the whole company for a full sync.

tenantAdmin.title: Tenant administrators
tenantAdmin.hint: Each enterprise tenant (tenant key = corp ID) gets an admin account automatically on provisioning, used to manage that tenant's org chart, members and roles. It is a tenant-level admin and cannot see other enterprises. The initial password is random and known to no one — to take over, reset a password you know here, hand it to the tenant admin, and they will be forced to change it on first login.
tenantAdmin.resetHint: This resets the tenant admin password of enterprise {{corpId}}. Choose the new password yourself and deliver it out-of-band — only a bcrypt hash is stored, so no existing password can ever be shown. The admin must change it on first login, and their existing sessions are revoked immediately.

mcp.title: MCP Service Management
mcp.descriptionSource: Tool descriptions are authored by solution publishers; whether to expose them to agents is the admin's call.

guide.unmounted: Steps: 1) set enabled to true inside the existing server.mcp section of config.yaml (skeleton preinstalled); 2) trigger hot reload: POST {base}/_system/config (loopback or Bearer); 3) refresh this page.
guide.auth: Check the mcp auth settings: make sure the auth plugin and allow_anonymous match the browser login session — {base}/mcp shares the same JWT auth surface as this site's API.
guide.unreachable: If the message above says canonical_origin is missing: fill vars.canonical_origin in config.yaml with the site's real public address, then refresh; if it says the network is unreachable: check the oj service process and port.

mcp.mountedAlert: Whitelist enabled: only solution-module tools are exposed; installing a solution registers it automatically; tools from non-solution modules never appear in this catalog.

group.drift: No visible tools (not whitelisted, or no api)

mcp.tokenExp: Credentials: the Bearer JWT comes from your browser login (expires in about 24 hours; expired calls return 401). Agent static config never refreshes it automatically — paste a fresh one when it expires. Long-lived credentials come in a later release.
mcp.reconnect: How changes apply: the catalog is fixed at connection time — after install/upgrade/uninstall, agents must reconnect to see the latest tools; calling an old offline tool mid-session returns -32601.
mcp.paramsShape: Argument shape: tool arguments are always nested path/query/body objects.
mcp.lineA: Route A (offline codegen, an ops action outside the site): oj mcp -c config.yaml generates a dependency-free stdio server (env OJ_BASE / OJ_TOKEN / OJ_TENANT). It is a file snapshot — regenerate after solution changes.

token.hint: A service token (svc token) is used only for OBO exchange: the bot trades it for a 10-minute delegated token. Real authority comes from the bound employee's own roles. The plaintext is shown only once, at issuance.
token.name: Name
token.scopeHint: read = GET; write = POST/PUT/PATCH; destructive = DELETE. Never grant destructive to a bot; also enable act_mask_destructive to mask delete tools.
token.ttlDaysHint: 0 = long-lived (system cap 90 days, rotate before expiry); 1–90 = custom days.
token.onceHint: The plaintext token is shown only once and cannot be retrieved after closing. Copy it into the bot's server-side secret store (e.g. vars.WECOM_BOT_SVC_TOKEN) — never into code or logs.
token.revokeConfirm: Revoking removes the jti from the registry immediately (cache settles in ~30s). Continue?

binding.hint: A binding maps an IM channel account to a site user. On OBO exchange the bot looks up the employee by (provider, external_sub); the delegated token carries that employee's own roles.
binding.deleteConfirm: Delete this binding? The employee can no longer be represented by the bot.
binding.importHint: The CSV header must be provider,external_sub,user_id; a repeated (provider, external_sub) updates the row (upsert). The export button downloads the same format and can be imported back.

audit.hint: Every OBO exchange (success or failure) writes one audit row. Failure reasons help diagnose unbound accounts, revoked credentials, or disabled users.

reason.not_svc: Not a svc credential (missing bot role)
reason.unbound: Account not bound for bot delegation

guide.tenantNote: This template has tenant strong-binding enabled (require_signed_claim): the bot credential (svc token) is issued by this tenant's admin on this page, and the token already embeds this tenant's claim. The callback / OBO exchange (/auth/obo) / tool calls (/mcp tools/call) only need to present this Bearer credential — oj treats the token's tenant claim as the request tenant, so the X-TENANT-ID header must match it, or be omitted so the framework derives it from the token. The devkit mcp-bot-guide sample defaults to single-tenant with no such claim, so make sure you use the svc token issued by this tenant, otherwise it is rejected with 403 tenant header does not match signed claim.
guide.mcpHint: The template ships with server.mcp.enabled: false (fail-closed). Enable it on the MCP Services page before the bot can reach {base}/mcp; installing a solution auto-registers its name into the modules allowlist, and only allowlisted tools are exposed. The 'Plugin Config' tab generates the WeCom-side plugin config for you.
guide.botHint: A WeCom normal-mode bot becomes callable by everyone via one MCP plugin. The plugin URL goes through this template's in-process proxy /api/wecom-bot/mcp (the same path is shared across tenants; the tenant is chosen by the Bearer). The 'Plugin Config' tab already generates a copyable config block for the current tenant.
guide.steps:
① On the Service Tokens tab, issue an svc token for this tenant (read/write, not destructive).
② Switch to the Plugin Config tab, pick the token you just issued, and copy the generated plugin config.
③ In the WeCom admin console, create an MCP plugin: type MCP, transport Streamable HTTP, URL = /api/wecom-bot/mcp under this tenant's enterprise domain.
④ Auth method = Service token (Header); set Authorization to Bearer <plaintext token>; set Content-Type and Accept exactly as in the config block.
⑤ X-WeCom-User-Id is auto-injected by WeCom under the enterprise domain — do not fill it; do not set X-TENANT-ID.
⑥ @-mention the bot in WeCom and verify it lists tools and calls them successfully; an OBO Audit success row should appear.
guide.checklist:
□ An svc token is issued for this tenant, without destructive scope, with a known ttl_days (long-lived = 90d, rotate on expiry).
□ An MCP plugin is created in WeCom: URL under the enterprise domain, transport Streamable HTTP, Authorization = Bearer <token>.
□ Content-Type=application/json and Accept=application/json, text/event-stream are set exactly.
□ server.mcp.enabled is on and the modules allowlist contains the needed solutions.
□ act_mask_destructive: true is on so delete tools are masked for the bot.
□ The token's days-left is watched on the expiry dashboard; rotate when within 30 days (avoids the K6 availability risk).
□ A real @-mention succeeded and shows an OBO Audit success row.
guide.codes:
40310 Unbound: no binding row for (provider, external_sub).
40311 Revoked: jti missing or absent from the oj_svc_token registry (fail-closed).
40312 Not a svc credential: claims.svc missing, or token lacks the bot role.
40313 Disabled: the bound user does not exist or has is_forbidden=1.
guide.security:
The svc token only covers the exchange hop and grants no business authority by itself; the delegated token's roles are read live from sys_user_role (the employee's own roles) and expire in 10 minutes.
Revocation uses the jti's presence in oj_svc_token as the source of truth, checked on every exchange (~30s cache).
The delegated token's claims.act.sub points back to the svc name; act_mask_destructive masks delete operations on that basis, and every exchange leaves an audit row.

plugin.tenantNote: A normal-mode bot (one per tenant) is onboarded by adding an MCP plugin in the WeCom admin console: the URL must live under this tenant's enterprise domain, so WeCom injects the employee identity on tools/call. The tenant is chosen by the Bearer below, not encoded in the URL.
plugin.pickerHint: Pick a service token issued by this tenant (issue it on the Service Tokens tab). After copying the config, paste the plaintext Bearer into Authorization. One token = one tenant's entry point.
plugin.writeScopeWarn: The selected token has no write scope. The bot calls tools on behalf of employees (a write surface), and the gateway requires the write scope for /wecom-bot/mcp — without it the real plugin is silently rejected with 403. Pick another token or issue one that includes write.
plugin.configTitle: WeCom plugin config (paste into WeCom console)
plugin.configHint: Fill the WeCom MCP plugin config item by item from this text. Replace the Bearer value in Authorization with the plaintext token issued on the Service Tokens tab after copying.
plugin.headerNote: Note: X-WeCom-User-Id is auto-injected by WeCom under the enterprise domain — do not fill it manually; do not set X-TENANT-ID (tenant is derived from the Bearer; a mismatch is rejected with 403). If 'Service token' rejects the space-prefixed value, fall back to 'No auth' and put Authorization in the request header.

maintenance.title: Danger zone: resource cleanup
maintenance.desc: When uninstalling the bot integration or resetting a tenant, wipe this tenant's three bot tables in one call. This is irreversible and scoped to the current tenant only.
maintenance.list: Will delete: oj_svc_token (service tokens — every plugin stops working immediately), oj_bot_binding (employee bindings), oj_obo_audit (OBO audit records).
maintenance.limits: Not affected: already-issued OBO tokens are stateless 10-minute JWTs that cannot be revoked individually (valid up to 10 minutes); the gateway caches deleted credentials for up to 30 seconds. Module code, routes and permissions are out of scope (use solution uninstall).
maintenance.ack: I understand these records will be permanently deleted
maintenance.confirmDesc: Service tokens, employee bindings and OBO audit records will be deleted and cannot be restored.
maintenance.cleanupOk: Cleaned up: {{svc_tokens}} service tokens / {{bindings}} bindings / {{audit_rows}} audit rows
